answer.rationale: Write-path latency spike (5x target, 90 minutes) coinciding with a release 2 hours ago in the primary region during peak settlement traffic suggests the release introduced a regression. Memory b1 demonstrates rollback cleared a checkout error spike without customer impact using the prior stable build. Memory b6 shows staged release gating can catch regressions early. A rollback preserves all writes, avoids abandoning the release entirely before investigation, and restores known-good code fastest under peak load. Regional failover (b2) would work but costs complexity during settlement peak; capacity adds time we don't have; circuit breakers (b4) and read routing (b5) don't address write-path latency. Verifying b1 confirms rollback success criteria and timing. Testing rollback on a small gated cohort first mitigates risk if the release is not the root cause.
